text:
1. When this chapter is set beside the earlier promise, the difference between them narrows.
2. The chapter reminds readers that Isaac is the child of the covenant.
3. Isaac is the one through whom the nations are to be blessed.
4. The chapter turns the covenant promise into a test.
5. The scene hinges on the single Hebrew word "hineni."
6. "Hineni" means "here I am."
7. Abraham speaks "hineni" three times in the scene.
8. Abraham says "hineni" once to God, once to Isaac, and once to the angel.
9. Each time Abraham says "hineni," the word means something different.
10. Each time Abraham says "hineni," it costs him more than the time before.
11. Being present to God and to others in this scene is inseparable from loss.
